title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 7th Congressional District
area: The Lehigh Valley and part of the Poconos: Lehigh and Northampton counties and part of Monroe County.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground. Both parties have won the district since 2020: Joe Biden (D) carried it 50%-49% in 2020, Donald Trump (R) carried it 51%-48% in 2024, and Ryan Mackenzie defeated then-incumbent Susan Wild 50%-49% in 2024. As of June 30, 2026, candidates and satellite groups had spent $9.4 million on the race.

Bob Brooks defeated Ryan Crosswell, Lamont McClure, and Carol Obando-Derstine in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary, winning 41.0% of the vote. Ryan Mackenzie was unopposed in the Republican primary.
Andrew Tupone (Green Party), Ramon Granados (Independent), and Frank Golden (Unaffiliated) withdrew or did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

summary.text: Ryan Mackenzie is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 7th District, first elected in 2024 after defeating then-incumbent Susan Wild. He previously served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2012 to 2024. He chairs a subcommittee of the House Committee on Education and the Workforce and also serves on the Homeland Security and Foreign Affairs committees.

background.text: Graduated from Parkland High School in 2000, earned a B.S. in finance and international business from New York University in 2004, and an M.B.A. from Harvard University in 2010.
Served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives representing District 134 (2012-2022) and District 187 (2022-2024) before being elected to Congress in 2024.
Has served on the Aggregate Advisory Board, the Pennsylvania Economic Development Financing Authority, and the Pennsylvania Workforce Development Board.

priorities.text: Campaign platform lists 12 priorities, including delivering tax relief, safeguarding Social Security and Medicare, improving housing affordability, reducing health care costs, and securing the border.

Says his first package of bills in Congress included proposals on the Child Tax Credit and childcare tax credits, some of which were included in the "Working Families Tax Cuts," and that he continues to work "across the aisle to support a host of commonsense legislative initiatives that make life easier for working families."
priorities.quote: The very first package of bills Ryan introduced in Congress included proposals to the Child Tax Credit, childcare tax credits, and more. While Congressman Mackenzie was able to include these ideas in the Working Families Tax Cuts, he's not done yet – continuing to team with legislators from across the aisle to support a host of commonsense legislative initiatives that make life easier for working families.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on reducing the cost of living through housing, transportation, and energy permitting legislation.
priorities.quote: We're continuing to work on housing legislation, transportation legislation, energy permitting legislation. All those things can help bring down costs in the long-term.

positions.summary: Campaign platform says he delivered tax relief for "every American," including increasing the standard deduction and eliminating taxes on Social Security for most seniors, and opposes raising taxes; does not campaign on raising taxes on high earners.
positions.quote: Ryan Mackenzie worked so hard to deliver tax relief for every American in his first year in Congress – from increasing the standard tax deduction to eliminating taxes on Social Security for nearly 90% of seniors.

positions.summary: Says he passed "the largest-ever expansion of affordable housing tax credits," intended to help create over one million new affordable housing units nationwide, and will continue to support policies to improve housing affordability.
positions.quote: was successful in passing the largest-ever expansion of affordable housing tax credits, which will help to create over one million new affordable housing units nationwide

positions.summary: Campaign says he "secured America's border from illegal immigration" through his work on the Homeland Security Committee and helped secure resources to combat human trafficking and drug smuggling.
positions.quote: Ryan Mackenzie finally secured America's border from illegal immigration through his work on the Homeland Security Committee.

positions.summary: Says he opposed cuts to Social Security and voted to increase Medicare funding, and passed legislation targeting insurance-company and middleman costs, but campaigns on lowering costs rather than expanding public coverage.
positions.quote: In Congress, Ryan refused to support any budget that reduced Social Security benefits. He also voted to invest more in Medicare every year – no cuts.

positions.summary: Says he has secured millions of dollars to support law enforcement and first responders and will continue to work with law enforcement on public-safety legislation.
positions.quote: he has secured millions of dollars to better support law enforcement and first responders, as well as passed important laws that secure our borders and combat the illegal drug trade

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on Education and the Workforce (where he chairs a subcommittee), and the Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 2025-2026 Congress.
Says he introduced a package of bills including proposals for an expanded Child Tax Credit and childcare tax credits, and that provisions were incorporated into the "Working Families Tax Cuts."
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, defeating incumbent Susan Wild 50.4% to 49.4%.

candidates.name: Bob Brooks
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary with 41.0% of the vote
candidates.currentRole: Former President, Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association

summary.text: Bob Brooks is a former Bethlehem firefighter (2005-2025) and former president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association. He won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary and is running against incumbent Ryan Mackenzie, campaigning on affordability, health care, and opposition to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

background.text: Worked as a firefighter in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, from 2005 to 2025.
Elected president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association in 2021.
Started Brooks Lawn Care, a snow removal and lawn care business, in 2013, and is a youth and varsity baseball coach at Nazareth Area High School.

priorities.text: Lists affordability, health care (restoring Medicaid cuts and "Medicare for All"), housing, childcare, and utilities as his three key campaign messages, along with protecting Social Security and enforcing antitrust rules.
priorities.quote: The number one thing I hear from folks is how expensive life is. People can't keep up with groceries, rent, healthcare, childcare, or utility bills. Wages aren't keeping up, and too many are working harder than ever for too little.

priorities.text: Says he wants to take money out of politics, end stock trading in Congress, enforce term limits, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.
priorities.quote: We need to take money out of politics, end stock trading in Congress, enforce term limits, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.

priorities.text: Names wages, safe working conditions, the social safety net, health care, and affordable housing as the public-policy areas he is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Supports restoring Medicaid cuts made under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and providing "Medicare for All."
positions.quote: Healthcare: Restore Medicaid cuts and provide Medicare for All.

positions.summary: Says the wealthy should "pay their fair share" and supports enforcing antitrust rules to stop price-gouging.
positions.quote: We need to take money out of politics, end stock trading in Congress, enforce term limits, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Supports building more market-rate homes, banning private equity from driving up housing costs, and extending VA-style home loans to essential workers.
positions.quote: Housing: Build more market-rate homes, ban private equity from driving up costs, and extend VA-style home loans to essential workers.

positions.summary: Supports repealing Head Start cuts and expanding childcare subsidies and publicly funded preschool.
positions.quote: Childcare: Repeal Headstart cuts, expand subsidies and publicly funded preschool.

candidates.researchNotes: No official record items included; Brooks has not held elected office. Positions are drawn from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
